exposure: Insulin (0.8-0.9 mg/kg/day in two divided doses subcutaneously)
outcome: Cesarean sections due to feto-maternal disproportion
Glycemic control (FBS and HbA1C before and after treatment)
cohort: The study included 71 GDM-diagnosed females meeting WHO criteria, divided into two groups for metformin or insulin treatment.
finding: Metformin demonstrated better effects on feto-maternal outcomes and glycemic control compared to insulin in GDM patients, with newborns in the insulin group being significantly heavier and having a higher incidence of cesarean sections.
mod_finding: There was a significantly higher number of cesarean sections due to feto-maternal disproportion in the insulin-treated group (28%) compared to the metformin-treated group (2%).
birth_weight: Newborns in the insulin group were significantly more in weight (p=0.01).
gest_age: Significant numbers of babies were delivered after 38 weeks of pregnancy in the insulin group (P=0.021).
